"''Thank you, my friend.|Sabé and Padmé Amidala|}} '''Sabé''' {{Pronounced|sɑ'beɪ}}, formerly known as '''Tsabin''', was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[planet]] [[Naboo]] during the [[Republic Era|late era]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. Serving as a [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|handmaiden]] in the [[Royal House of Naboo]], Sabé was duty-bound to protect [[Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]]—the [[Democracy|elected]] [[Monarch of Naboo|ruler]] of the [[Naboo (people)|people of Naboo]]—against any threat. As such, she impersonated Amidala during the [[Invasion of Naboo]] in order to keep her safe from the [[Trade Federation]], and continued to do so after the queen and her royal retinue were [[Capture of Theed|rescued]] by the [[Jedi]] [[ambassador]]s [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. It was only when Amidala herself personally requested the help of [[Boss]] [[Rugor Nass]] and his [[Gungan]] [[Gungan Grand Army|warriors]] that Sabé's disguise was revealed. Sabé proved instrumental in ending the ensuing [[Battle of Naboo]], diverting [[Nute Gunray]]'s [[battle droid]]s to allow Amidala and her [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]] the opportunity to [[Prisoner|capture]] the Federation [[Viceroy]]. Sabé continued to serve as Amidala's handmaiden, decoy, and loyal [[bodyguard]] throughout her two terms as [[queen]]. When Amidala made the decision to represent Naboo's [[Chommell sector]] in the [[Galactic Senate]] of the Republic, Sabé followed, but not before being sent on a mission to the planet [[Tatooine]]. Alongside Security Force [[Captain]] [[Tonra]], Sabé was able to relocate a number of [[Slavery|slaves]] to the planet [[Karlinus]], but was unsuccessful in locating [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], a woman that Amidala had met four years prior and hoped to rescue. Returning to the former queen's side on [[Coruscant]], Sabé stood by Amidala through the political chaos of the [[Separatist Crisis]]. Following Amidala's mysterious [[death]] after the [[Mission to Mustafar|end]] of the [[Clone Wars]] and the [[Proclamation of the New Order|birth]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Sabé and Tonra changed their identities and began an investigation to discover how their beloved [[senator]] and friend had died. Together with a group of Naboo loyalists known as the [[Amidalans]], they discovered the involvement of [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], who unknown to all was actually Anakin Skywalker, Shmi's son and Amidala's secret [[Marriage|husband]]. Sabé began a quest of revenge against Vader that lasted into the [[Galactic Civil War]] and saw her [[Spy|infiltrate]] the ranks of criminal syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]]. After multiple encounters with the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], Sabé eventually uncovered enough clues to piece together the true identity of Vader, throwing her into the dangerous path of the former [[Jedi Knight]]. ==Biography== ===Early life=== {{Quote|Your teachers say you are diligent. You are never late. You are scrupulous when it comes to performing your part, and your conduct is near perfect at all times. And yet you are always second best. At everything you have ever tried.|Quarsh Panaka to Tsabin|}} Tsabin was [[Reproduction|born]] on [[Naboo]] around [[46 BBY]], into a family of [[Seven-string hallikset|hallikset]] players. As per family tradition, she was sent to study [[music]] at the [[Theed Conservatory]], a school known for training traditional [[musician]]s, as her older brothers had studied there. Though she hid it well, she strongly disliked following the path laid out for her, with no hope of anything more than a supporting role in any orchestra on Naboo. In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Queen's Peril]]'' to [[32 BBY]].'' the year she turned fourteen and was old enough to vote, Tsabin was expected to take up an apprenticeship, she was approached by [[Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka]] of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]], who asked her to hold off on accepting an apprenticeship until after the upcoming election, although he provided no details. Tsabin, looking up the candidates running for [[queen]], discovered that she had a strong resemblance to one of the candidates, the girl called [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Amidala]], and suspected what Panaka might have in mind. ===Preparations=== ====First days==== {{Quote|I think the queen and her new handmaiden are up to something."
"They're teenage girls. They are always going to be up to something.|Quarsh and Mariek Panaka|}} After Amidala won the election, Tsabin accepted Panaka's offer to be trained as her body double. She was introduced to Amidala, who entrusted her with her given name, Padmé, and officially became the [[Monarch of Naboo|Queen of Naboo's]] first [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|handmaiden]] as a cover. The two discussed Panaka's plan for Tsabin to act as both a decoy and a bodyguard for Amidala, and Tsabin proposed to the queen that all handmaidens should be solely loyal to her rather than Panaka, feeling that doing so was the only way to truly keep the Queen safe. In the early days after Amidala's election, before the official transfer of power at the [[Day of Ascendancy]], Tsabin and Amidala shared a room in the [[Theed Royal Palace|palace]]. Despite growing pains as Amidala struggled to balance her roles as queen and friend when relating to Tsabin, the two managed to conceive a detailed plan for how Amidala's staff of handmaidens would protect and conceal the queen. Tsabin taught Amidala the breath control exercises hallikset players learned to help conceal her emotions; this gave the Queen a flat, monotone voice and inflection that would be easy for Tsabin to mimic. Amidala, in turn, made sure Tsabin was familiar with her personal mannerisms. Panaka, meanwhile, worried that their plotting together without including him would make it harder to protect Amidala. At the end of the week, Tsabin helped Amidala prepare for her Ascendancy, painting the [[Scar of remembrance|royal symbols]] onto her face for the first time. While the new queen approached the [[Sanandrassa|former queen]], her first handmaiden faded into the background in [[robe]]s dyed to match her queen's [[Clothing|dress]]. Tsabin and Amidala moved to the royal apartments that day, where the two intended to share the largest bedroom. There, Amidala pushed back against Panaka's security recommendations for the first time when he asked to have his men stationed in her quarters. After a tense moment, he assented to Tsabin's plan of having only the handmaidens present in the royal apartments and arranged for them to receive combat training and military conditioning. ====All pieces in play==== {{Quote|Rabene Tonsort, gifted artist and actress. Eirtama Ballory, scientist and engineer; Suyan Higin, seamstress and maker; and Sashah Adova-|Panaka, introducing Tasbin's fellow handmaidens, to herself and Amidala.|}} [[File:Shatterpoint-WeAreBravewallpaper.png|thumb|right|250px|Sabé (left) with Queen Padmé Amidala]] Two weeks after Amidala assumed power, Panaka presented four other girls, [[Rabé Tonsort|Rabene Tonsort]], [[Eirtaé|Eirtama Ballory]], [[Yané|Suyan Higin]], and [[Saché|Sashah Adova]], to her as potential handmaidens as well, and the Queen took them to her apartments in the [[Theed Royal Palace]] for a private discussion. There, Amidala shared her personal name with them, and the girls decided what roles each would have in Amidala's service. At Tonsort's suggestion, the handmaidens changed their names as Amidala had for privacy, as a symbol of their devotion to the Queen, and so if Amidala was disguised as a handmaiden it would be less noticeable; with similar names, they would be more forgettable. The last to pick her new name, Tsabin became "Sabé". During a [[Chommell sector summit|summit]] hosted by Amidala on Naboo for the leaders of the planet in the [[Chommell sector]], Sabé met [[Harli Jafan]], the daughter of [[Jafan]]'s [[Harli Jafan's father|planetary director]], who had sent his daughter as an [[ambassador]] in his place. During this time, Sabé and Harli became close and developed romantic feelings for one another. Later, Harli invited Sabé and her friends to see the band [[Neurotransmitter Affection]], who were playing at the [[Theed Odeon]]. Although Harli most likely just meant Sabé's fellow handmaidens, Amidala also came in disguise, with the youngest handmaiden, Saché, staying behind at the palace due to a stomach ache. While at the concert Sabé danced with Harli, but eventually Sabé, the other handmaidens, and Amidala were forced to return to the palace as Panaka had learnt of the girls sneaking out from Saché, whose [[period]] had accidentally set off the [[blood-sensitive sensor]] in Amidala's bedroom. The next day, the handmaidens were unable to remove the glitter on Amidala's hand from the [[glitter-lit]] that had broken on her the night before. As the handmaidens did not wish for anyone to know that the queen had snuck out and wearing [[glove]]s would be offensive to the delegates from [[Kreeling]], Sabé was forced to assume the role of the Queen for the first time. At the end of the day, Sabé received a hurtful note from Harli who had mistaken the disguised Amidala for Sabé and had attempted to kiss her only for Amidala to recoil. Sabé, realising what had happened, confronted Amidala on ruining her budding relationship by hurting Harli, which caused a temporary rift between the two. ===Invasion of Naboo=== ====Flight from Theed==== {{Quote|Padmé. Clean this droid up the best you can. It deserves our gratitude.|Sabé, as Queen Amidala|}} [[File:SabeRabePadme-TPM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Sabé impersonated Queen Amidala in order to protect her during the Invasion of Naboo.]] Sabé was in service to Queen Amidala during the [[Trade Federation]]'s [[blockade]] and subsequent [[invasion of Naboo]]. As the blockade began and the possibility of Naboo coming under direct military attack grew, Amidala gave Sabé her [[Padmé Amidala's locket|locket]] but instructed her to give it back once the crisis was over. When Federation forces captured the Theed Royal Palace, Sabé was quickly dressed in the Queen's formal gown and makeup, with Amidala, using her true name of Padmé, wearing her handmaiden's disguise. Sabé, as Amidala, rejected [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]'s efforts to have her sign a treaty that would make the invasion legal. She and the rest of the royal retinue were then escorted by [[B1-series battle droid|battle droids]] to a separate holding facility to be processed as prisoners of war. On the way, they were rescued by [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. Proceeding to a nearby [[hangar]], Jinn insisted that the queen be taken to [[Coruscant]] to plead her case to the [[Galactic Senate]]. After conferring with Padmé by pretending to ask her a question, Sabé agreed to leave her people in the care of Governor [[Sio Bibble]]. She subsequently left Naboo aboard the [[Naboo Royal Starship|Royal Starship]] with the [[Jedi]], taking Padmé, Panaka, Eirtaé and Rabé with her. Despite coming under fire from the Federation blockade, the ship's crew managed to pilot the Queen and her entourage safely out of the [[Naboo system]]. Sabé—as the queen—commended maintenance droid [[R2-D2]] for pulling off a dangerous repair to the [[Starship|ship]] during its escape, and ordered Padmé to clean the [[astromech droid]]. However, the Royal Starship's [[hyperdrive]] was heavily damaged. Forced to land on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], Sabé remained on the starship while Jinn and Padmé sought a new [[T-14 hyperdrive generator]]. When they reached the [[The galaxy|galactic]] [[capital]] of Coruscant, Sabé was initially presented as the queen to [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum|Valorum]] and [[Senator]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], who represented Naboo in the Galactic Congress. Padmé then reassumed her responsibilities as Queen and was formally prepared for her address to the Senate by Sabé and her fellow handmaidens. ====Negotiations with the Gungans==== {{Quote|Viceroy! Your occupation here has ended.|Sabé, as Queen Amidala|}} [[File:ArmedAndFabulous-TPM.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Sabé continued to serve as Amidala's decoy during the Battle of Naboo.]] Sabé once again switched places with Amidala when they sought help from [[Gungan]] [[Gungan Grand Army|forces]], and began negotiations with their leader, [[Boss]] [[Rugor Nass|Nass]]. However, Padmé saw that Nass was resistant to trusting the people of Naboo, and chose to reveal the deception as a confidence-building measure; the two parties finally agreed to work together in order to free their planet from the Trade Federation. Despite being exposed, Sabé remained disguised as Queen Amidala during the [[Battle of Naboo|mission]] to reclaim the palace. When Padmé was [[Prisoner|captured]], she played an instrumental role in deceiving [[Viceroy]] Gunray. Showing up suddenly at the door to the throne room, Sabe proclaimed the Viceroy's occupation over and blasted two of his droids before fleeing with her group. Gunray ordered his [[troop]]s to follow Sabé, believing she was the real queen. This provided Padmé the opportunity to retrieve a [[blaster]] hidden in the throne's armrest and take the [[Neimoidian]] into custody, liberating the planet. Sabé was later present when the queen welcomed Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]] to Naboo, and at the parade celebrating the freedom of Naboo and the reconciliation of its human and Gungan populations. With the invasion over Sabé attempted to return Amidala's locket to her as instructed but Amidala had since changed her mind and told Sabé to keep it as a thanks from a planet that would never fully appreciate what she'd done. Instead, Amidala's token became the [[japor snippet]] gifted to her by [[Anakin Skywalker]] on the trip to Coruscant. In [[28 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Queen's Shadow]]'' to [[28 BBY]].'' Sabé was present when Amidala decided against a recommendation from her council to revise Naboo's [[Constitution of Naboo|constitution]] and remove the two-term limit imposed on all Queens, acknowledging that though popular sentiment favored her being given a third term, it was essential that Naboo's democratic traditions be respected. Sabé later asked Amidala if she was tempted to stay in office, which Amidala responded that of course she was tempted but also knew that it was wrong to do so. The pair never spoke of it again. ===Service to the senator and mission to Tatooine=== ====Serving a senator==== {{Dialogue|Amidala|I had thought I would go back to Tatooine, to help the people there.|Eirtaé|You could have more of an impact if you were in the Senate. You could help more planets than just Tatooine.|Yané|The Senate takes years to get anything done. You would get more done with a good ship and connections on Tatooine itself.|Sabé|If only, you knew of a way to be in two places at once.|attr=Padmé Amidala, Eirtaé, Yané, and Sabé|src=}} Sabé, along with the other handmaidens, several members of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]], Quash, and [[Mariek Panaka]] stayed with Amidala at [[Varykino Villa]] during the elections when Amidala's second term as queen had ended and was present for the announcements of Saché being elected to Naboo's [[Naboo planetary legislative assembly|planetary legislative assembly]] and the election of former Queen [[Réillata]] as Amidala's successor. Sabé was also present for the [[second coronation of Réillata]] and saw the new queen offer Amidala the chance to succeed the retiring [[Senator]] [[Oshadam]] in representing the Chommell sector in the Galactic Republic. After Amidala left the [[throne]], Sabé was the only former member of the royal household to remain in employment to her. Among other tasks, Amidala sent Sabé back to Tatooine in an effort to free [[Slavery|slaves]], having learned of the planet's widespread and illegal trade during her travels to the Senate. Although Amidala had specifically requested that Sabé locate [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], the handmaiden could not find her. She brought the slaves she did free to a new life on the planet [[Karlinus]] financed personally by Amidala. She was helped by former royal guardsman Tonra, with whom she began an on-again, off-again relationship. Sabé and Tonra then returned to Coruscant, where Amidala was beginning her senatorial career. After discovering that Senator [[Mon Mothma]], a leader of the Senate's opposition to Chancellor Palpatine and his pro-military agenda, planned to stage a distraction at a party she was hosting in order to have a secret discussion with her allies, Sabé put on one of the Senator's outfits and faked a drunken spill of [[Toniray]] to distract the press and guests; with Amidala dressed in Sabé clothes and keeping an eye out, Mothma freely discussed her suspicions about Senator [[Mina Bonteri]] with Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan]] and Senator [[Onaconda Farr]] of [[Rodia]], whom Sabé was familiar with. Seeking to put her combat experience to use, Sabé enlisted as [[Hazard One]] in [[Hazard Squadron]], an anti-piracy [[starfighter]] [[squadron]] set up by the Galactic Republic to protect starship [[convoy]]s transporting materials to [[Bromlarch]] as part of the [[Mid Rim Cooperation Motion]]. Sabé and Tonra also began to spend more time apart than they did together, with Sabé often away on assignments building an intelligence network for Amidala while Tonra was working more closely with [[Gregar Typho]] and Mariek Panaka on the senator's protective detail. Usually, they only met up for a specific operation that Amidala was running or because Sabé needed backup. They spent time with others. By [[22 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' a handmaiden named [[Cordé]] had taken over Sabé's former role as Amidala's decoy, but she, along with a fellow handmaiden named [[Versé]], were killed by a bomb planted [[plot to assassinate Senator Amidala|to assassinate the Senator]].{{Film|II}} ====Shadow no more==== {{Quote|You and Padmé."
"It's none of your business."
"I am in my nightgown, and you are in my room. I think it's at least part of my business.|Sabé and Anakin Skywalker|}} As the [[Clone Wars]] erupted in 22 BBY, Sabé returned to Tatooine with Tonra after Amidala, frustrated by the Senate's inaction in stopping the slave trade, asked them to set up a permanent route for slaves to escape the planet to freedom. As cover, they assumed the false identities of "Sabon and Arton Dakellen", impoverished [[Merchant|traders]] who had come to Tatooine seeking work. Sabé found a job at a local water depot while Tonra became a cook at a [[cantina]], a post who allowed him to obtain food cheaply and to mix it with his own [[Spice (seasoning)|seasonings]]. After some time passed, they managed to establish a presence in the local community and were able to start setting up the anti-slavery route. Amidala then unexpectedly contacted Sabé, and asked her to return to Coruscant. The senator planned to conduct a secret investigation into a company suspected of war profiteering, and to keep from being discovered needed Sabé to not only assume her identity but her senatorial duties as well. Though Sabé found herself feeling a bit resentful due to the secretive way Amidala had been acting since the [[First Battle of Geonosis|Battle of Geonosis]], she agreed and return to Coruscant. While studying up on her new responsibilities, Sabé learned how much the Amidala role had changed, with her becoming more isolated due to security concerns, the handmaidens [[Ellé]] and [[Moteé]] being forced to sleep outside of her chambers, the staff having a more rigid routine with less interactivity, Amidala's evenings being specifically free of obligations, and no longer having dinners with her security personnel. After returned from a soirée hosted by Bail Organa at [[Cantham House]], she was awoken by Anakin Skywalker after Skywalker snuck into [[Padmé's Apartment]] during the night but found Sabé in her place. This caused Sabé to realize that the changes to her friends household were in order to spend more time on her [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala|marriage]], though she didn't realize that it was a [[marriage]] and not an affair until after a conversation with Skywalker at a [[Unidentified Jedi Temple garden|garden]] in the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]]. While Sabé was there, the [[Sith Lord]] Darth Sidious (in his guise as Chancellor Palpatine) used the [[dark side of the Force]] to determine her true identity, which caused a [[Jedi Temple pool|pool]] in the garden to dry up. Worn down by her new role and uncomfortable with having to deceive Skywalker, she resolved to never again act in Amidala's shadow and told her as such upon her return, while also rebuking her for not revealing her secret marriage. The two eventually spent the night together laughing and thinking back on their friendship, but it became clear that their once-strong relationship was tarnished by Amidala taking her handmaiden's service for granted. Sabé swiftly returned to Tonra on Tatooine to continue the work of freeing slaves with the organization they had founded, the [[White Suns]]. ===Death of Padmé Amidala=== {{Quote|It doesn't make any sense! She wouldn't just ''die''. And an empire? Headed by Sheev Palpatine? Nothing about this makes sense!|Sabé|}} [[File:Frontfuneral.png|thumb|left|250px|Sabé attended the funeral of her former sovereign, Padmé Amidala, which took place in Theed.]] Despite their falling out, Sabé still considered Amidala her friend and kept up to date with her actions in the Senate. In [[19 BBY]], the Clone Wars came to an [[Mission to Mustafar|end]] after Palpatine [[Proclamation of the New Order|transitioned]] the Republic into the First [[Galactic Empire]]. After seeing her husband [[Duel in Palpatine's office|fall]] to the dark side, Amidala lost her will to live and [[Death|died]] after giving birth to her children, [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]] and [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia]].{{Film|III}} The [[Padmé Amidala's funeral|funeral]] took place in Theed shortly after, which was attended by Sabé and Padmé's other surviving handmaidens. Every handmaiden, including Sabé, barely spoke during the procession, as their grief was profound and difficult for outsiders to understand. Following Amidala's funeral, Sabé left to be alone with her thoughts. However, she was eventually startled by a knock on the door. Although she initially believed it might be one of her many enemies, she soon realized that it was Tonra. After letting Tonra in, Sabé finally let her emotions flow freely, conveying anger and confusion at Amidala's death and the formation of the new Empire, which she felt had destroyed everything Amidala had devoted her life to building. After her outburst, Tonra asked Sabé what she would do. Sabé thought to herself that if Tonra's question had come from her parents, they would've been asking what Sabé would do without Padmé. However, considering how well Tonra knew her, Sabé understood that he was asking what she would do in Amidala's memory. [[File:Declaration.png|thumb|right|250px|Amidala's death came as a surprise to Sabé, as did the ascension of the Galactic Empire under Sheev Palpatine.]] After consideration, Sabé told Tonra that she wanted to determine the truth of Amidala's death, starting on Coruscant, feeling a duty to honor her former Queen. Tonra, wanting the same thing as Sabé, asked if he could accompany her on her journey. Considering their previous compatibility in the field, Sabé agreed to Tonra's request but noted that they would need to completely reinvent themselves and abandon their former lives (including their work with the White Suns) to ensure complete secrecy. Tonra was willing to do so, and the pair began immediately organizing for their trip. Tonra informed Sabé that he would put together a means for them to leave Naboo in secret if she would take responsibility for crafting their new identities. She urged him to make use of whatever old favors they were still owed, since they would be useless once they cast aside their former identities. Sabé also realized that she would need to leave behind Amidala's locket as it was too distinctive in appearance. She decided to leave it somewhere safe until she could return for it. As Sabé started working on the IDs at her workstation, she briefly glanced over the files left to her by Amidala's office. A majority of these files were pertaining to the many years of work Amidala had put into improving the galaxy, as well as the policies she never had the chance to petition. As she looked them over, her emotions began to swell, and she sought to know more than ever why Amidala had died. Her contemplation was soon interrupted by her [[comm unit]] chiming, although Sabé decided not to answer it. Tonra answered it and insisted that Sabé talk to the caller. Sabé relented and accepted the call, which was being sent by Senator Organa. Sabé asked Organa what he wanted. Later, Sabé and her allies broke into [[Padmé's Apartment|Padmé's apartment]] on Coruscant and stole the chamber's security recordings. Believing there could be a clue on the recordings, Sabé attempted to decrypt the footage. However, before she could do so, the Empire showed its true colors. At Organa's request, Sabé agreed to become a field commander for anti-Imperial rebels. She hid the recordings on Naboo where they would be safe until Sabé could continue the investigation.[[Darth Vader (2020) 2|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 2]] ===Encountering the Dark Lord=== ====Meeting on Vendaxa==== {{Quote|I am ''Padmé Amidala…Queen…Senator…Daughter of Naboo''…back from the dead to haunt you to your grave.|Sabé to Darth Vader|}} [[File:DarthVaderMeetsSabe-2020DarthVader1.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Darth Vader encountered Sabé, who still bore a striking resemblance to the late Amidala.]] During the [[Galactic Civil War]], sometime after the [[Duel on Cloud City]] in [[3 ABY]], Sabé and her [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel]] squad were in a base on [[Vendaxa]] when the facility was breached by the local [[Vendaxan land squid]]s. Her team were swiftly massacred by the creatures. The last of Sabé's soldiers, a [[Unidentified Gungan soldier|Gungan]], requested that she evacuate the base. Sabé refused, as she didn't want to leave without the crew, and as such had to watch as the Gungan soldier was also killed by the land squids. When it seemed as though Sabé would be overrun, a dark figure entered the facility with a [[Darth Vader's lightsaber|lightsaber]] in hand. The man used his lightsaber to make quick work of the land squids, clearing the immediate vicinity of the creatures. Upon seeing Sabé, the man spoke the name "Padmé" in disbelief.[[Darth Vader (2020) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 1]] Sabé, who had her blaster trained on the man, demanded to know what he had just called her and who he was. A [[forensics droid]] that was accompanying the man remarked on the resemblance between Sabé and the deceased Padmé and introduced the man as [[Darth]] Vader, an agent of the Emperor. In response to the revelation that the dark figure was a servant of the Empire, Sabé immediately fired on Vader. However, the [[Sith Lord]] merely [[Force deflection|deflected]] the [[laser]] with [[the Force]] and [[Telekinesis|telekinetically]] disarmed Sabé. Vader inquired as to the identity of Sabé, who informed Vader that she was in fact Amidala, back to haunt him from the grave. Angered by Sabé's response, Vader used the Force to lift and [[Force choke|choke]] her. However, after a short while, Vader, who was secretly the former Jedi Anakin Skywalker, released her after experiencing memories of his deceased wife Amidala. Sabé grabbed her blaster and fled deeper into the facility, where the land squids still remained. When Vader followed, the squids attacked him, although he was still able to defeat them with relative ease. Hoping that the land squids could defeat Vader with enough numbers, Sabé deliberately opened a security gate in the facility that led into the main nest. Vader soon caught up with her and used the Force to prevent her from escaping. Vader again demanded to know Sabé's true identity, assuring her that she didn't have to be afraid of him. However, the handmaidens then came to Vader's aid, using their own magnetic devices to release him. While Tambor fled in a ship, the handmaidens unlocked Sabé's cage and insisted that she leave Vader's service. But Vader choked the handmaidens with the Force and asked Sabé if she wanted to allow Tambor to escape and leave the locals to suffer. [[File:VaderSabe-2020DarthVader32.png|thumb|right|250px|Having chosen him over her sisters, Sabé is safely brought to the ground by Darth Vader.]] Once they returned to base, the handmaidens insisted that Sabé leave with them and abandon the Empire. To this, Vader reiterated that she would only have the power to stop Tambor if she remained in his service. Vader then reached out his hand to Sabé. But before she could take it, Dormé tackled her out of the way while the rest of the handmaidens opened fire on Vader. They then took her outside and used their antigravity devices to fly her up toward their ship. When Sabé reminded them of Tambor's plans, the handmaidens assured her they would stop him together without Vader or the Empire. Realizing her fellow handmaidens would be outmatched and still wanting to fulfill Amidala's wish that the light existed in Vader, Sabé regretfully said goodbye before pulling away from the handmaidens and falling back down toward Vader, who caught her with the Force as they made their escape. Vader then called off his forces and returned to the ''Executor'' along with Sabé. While aboard the flagship, Vader and Sabé were informed of three gunships flying toward the planet's surface. When Vader redirected the reports to Sabé, as this was her mission, she asked how many life forms were aboard the gunships. As the crew said they would have to check, Sabé told them to prepare her shuttle. Figuring out a way to weaken Tambor's forces, she used her ship to gather twelve of the Skakoan refugees that Tambor had been assisting. She then contacted Tambor and told him that while Vader was at the Imperial base he was targeting, there were also Skakoan refugees there and that he should wait until Vader left the area. Tambor then asked how many refugees there were, to which she said twelve. Tambor then thanked Sabé for her help and had his gunships level the area. When Sabé accused Tambor of allowing his own people to die, Tambor said his people knew their place and that they would rejoice beneath his rule. Sabé then showed Tambor the very refugees she had been talking about. When she asked them if they would rejoice, they showed outrage at how Tambor had been willing to let them die. ====Chaos on the ''Executor''==== {{Quote|The other handmaidens ''fled''. But you are ''here''. ''Stronger''. And you will become ''stronger still''.''"
"''They only ''left''… because I kept my ''secret''. ''Your'' secret. If I'd told them what ''really'' happened… to ''Anakin Skywalker''… they would never have escaped. I know… my sisters… will always think of me with ''grief''… and they will always ''wonder'' what ''happened'' here… but they will go back to their ''lives''… and their ''loves''. This way… only ''one'' of us has to ''lose'' their ''soul''.|Darth Vader and Sabé|}} Following a [[Destruction of Jul's droid army|decisive victory]] over Tambor's droid forces, in which Sabé killed Gee-Ninety,[[Darth Vader (2020) 36|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 36]] Sabé reported to Vader on the ''Executor'' that the Skakoan refugees had abandoned Tambor's regime, discrediting him and leaving him powerless. Vader then asked Sabé how it felt to hold such power, to which she admitted that she didn't know what Amidala would do anymore. Vader then told her that she had chosen to be stronger while the rest of the handmaidens had fled. To this, Sabé explained that she hadn't informed them of Vader's true identity in order to ensure that they wouldn't have stayed and tried to kill him. Now, although their hearts were broken, they would continue to live their lives away from her and Vader. Sabé then said that this way, only one of them would lose their soul as she left Vader to meditate by himself. [[File:ExecutorChaos-2020DarthVader32.png|thumb|left|250px|Sabé reacts to sudden destruction aboard the ''Executor'' as Darth Vader loses control over the Force.]] However, as she walked from the room, Vader began to tear apart the ''Executor'' as he lost control over his [[Force power]]s because of the [[Force Wave]], which had returned after being first unleashed at the [[Battle at Amaxine Station|end of the Crimson Dawn war]].[[Hidden Empire 5|''Hidden Empire'' 5]] Sabé quickly realized Vader had lost control of the Force as the ship crumbled, ordering the officers and stormtroopers around her to clear the hallway and seal its doors, thereby throwing the out of control Vader into space. When an officer refused to, Sabé pushed past and did it herself, much to that officer's horror, before contacting Vader comlink to ask that he hold on for a moment. Instead, Vader, who was also dealing with Palpatine taunting him in his mind about whether he would turn his hate into power or suffering, Force choked Sabé before he was sucked out into space. Sabé quickly rushed to a ''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle and collected the Sith Lord's body with two [[Prowler 1000 seeker droid]]s. She also decided to bring Vader to an uninhabited [[Unidentified astronomical object (Sabé)|astronomical object]], where the Sith Lord could take his time in rediscovering his powers without hurting anyone. Although Sabé asked him to hold it back for just a minute longer, Vader's out of control powers destroyed the shuttle around him as they entered hyperspace, resulting in them crashing to the astronomical object once they exited hyperspace. Sabé quickly grabbed a wing backpack and jumped out of the crumbling ship to rescue the falling Vader, who grabbed her hand shortly before both crashed into the sea. Sabé lost her grip on Vader and sank beneath the waves. ====Power or suffering==== Sabé awoke on a beach and followed the footprints in the sand and path of destruction to Vader, who pushed the handmaiden back and demanded that she leave him behind. Sabé, instead, noted that she had specifically brought him to the astronomical object and offered that it could finally be a chance to take control of his life, calling him "Anakin" once more in the process. Vader unleashed a blast of energy that forced Sabé to throw herself back, only to grab her with the Force to turn the test his master had for him on her: out of hate, he demanded to know if she she would choose power or suffering. Sabé refused to answer and wanted to focus on figuring out a way for Vader to control his powers, but Vader brought her into an embrace and declared the only way to be safe was to remain in the center of the storm with him. At that moment, Vader allowed Sabé to see a [[Force vision]] of what he claimed was her own desires.[[Darth Vader (2020) 34|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 34]] [[File:SabeVision-2020DarthVader34.png|thumb|right|250px|Sabé experienced a vision where she chose to fully devote herself to the Empire.]] In the vision, Sabé chose power and used it to bring order to the galaxy upon fully embracing the Empire. In particular, she led the Empire in arresting Tambor and his remaining supporters, fought a group of slavers, and took part in the yet to occur{{Film|VI}} [[Battle of Endor]] against the Rebel Alliance, where her armor increasingly grew bloodied as she fired on her enemies. Returning to Naboo under the guard of two stormtroopers, she would then watch as her fellow Handmaidens and their family spoke to Padmé Amidala's tomb about Sabé's success. As she lived through the battle against the Rebels, however, she rejected the vision and confronted Vader, declaring that it was not the future she wanted for herself. One of her fellow Handmaidens tried to tell her Vader was not Anakin Skywalker when she asked him what he was doing, but Sabé chased after the Sith Lord after declaring he would always be Skywalker, no matter what he claimed. Instead of finding Vader, however, Sabé found visions of Amidala and Vader's son Luke, which she believed meant there was still good in Vader after all, just as Amidala had declared, as she believed she was within Vader's mind. Again claiming that it was Sabé's vision and not his own, Vader suddenly emerged and cut down both his wife and son before turning his blade against the Handmaidens, who tried to defend Sabé but were cut down while Vader declared the vision was filled with lies. When Vader offered her a new future by abandoning her past, Sabé rejected his offer and tumbled out of the vision, again trying to tell Vader to focus on controlling his powers. Instead, she was thrown back by Vader, who offered Sabé the choice to take either suffering or power one last time: as he noted, he would kill her if she defied him again simply because he could not control his greater-than-ever-before, but still out of control, power. Recoiling at the memory of Vader killing the illusions of his own wife and son, Sabé rejected the choice all together: she would simply refuse to hate. Sabé turned to walk away, which resulted in Vader throwing her out into the sea in his next blast of power. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|What I learned was that I'd rather be second to you than first to anyone else.''"
"''I can order you to your death.''"
"''And I would go.|Sabé and Padmé Amidala|}} [[File:Sabe-2024SWHyperspace.png|thumb|left|200px|Sabé was a human female who physically resembled Padmé Amidala.]] Like Amidala,{{Databank|padme-amidala|Padmé Amidala}} Sabé was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who stood at 1.65 [[meter]]s. She had [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], brown [[eye]]s, and light skin. Sabé was personally and professionally loyal to Queen Amidala, becoming her friend in addition to serving as her [[bodyguard]] and decoy in crisis situations despite the considerable risk of injury, capture, or even death. As a member of Amidala's royal retinue of handmaidens, Sabé was handpicked to aid the Queen of Naboo. Like all Naboo handmaidens, she learned self-defense and was also trained to remain vigilant against all threats to her monarch.{{Databank|naboo-royal-handmaidens|Naboo Royal Handmaidens}} When she impersonated the Queen and Amidala disguised herself as a handmaiden, the pair relied on a system of subtle signals in order to secretly communicate without undermining the deception of their switched roles. Having fallen in love with Amidala, Sabé's love and loyalty toward her friend led her to place Amidala's needs above those of any other beings, including her own, although she knew Amidala could not reciprocate. Although she once advised Amidala to return romantic love to someone who understood her, she was certain Amidala would never return her feelings and assumed her friend would chose something larger than a person to love, such as a planet or species, which left her shocked to discover she had married Anakin Skywalker. She preferred being Amidala's second to being first to anyone else, although this made it difficult to maintain relationships with lovers who could not understand that they would never be more important to her than Amidala; Tonra understood and accepted it before they became intimate, but her brief relationship with [[Harli Jafan]] did not last. Sabé was more often interested in fellow humans than beings of other species, though she sometimes found [[Alien|nonhumans]] attractive, usually if they were interesting females. [[File:VadersWeirdMarriageProposal-2020DarthVader31.png|thumb|right|250px|Sabé wanted to fulfill Padmé Amidala's dying words that good existed in Darth Vader, but needed to face a crossroads of her own by getting close to the Sith Lord.]] After joining with Darth Vader to foster and fulfill Amidala's belief that the light still existed within him, Sabé found herself at a crossroads of her own as her continued service to Vader and the Empire compromised her own morals. She saw she could dedicate herself fully to bringing Imperial order to the galaxy in the name of protecting those she loved and the innocent, but she only stayed with the Empire because of her devotion to redeeming Vader. Indeed, she saw all she did in his service as her losing her own soul, taking solace in the fact that her handmaiden sisters did not join her. During the Force Wave, Vader decided to test his new disciple by making her choose if she would turn her hatred into suffering or, in the choice that would bound her to his service, power. Vader even showed her a vision of herself as an effective Imperial commander who brought Imperial order to the galaxy, claiming it was her own wish. Sabé, however, rejected that future. When Vader demanded that she turn her hatred into either suffering or power one last time, she decided not to hate altogether. ==Skills and abilities== Sabé was a capable markswoman, taking off the head of a battle droid at one point with a single shot. ==Equipment== During her time as a handmaiden, Sabé carried a standard [[ELG-3A blaster pistol]] like the queen and her fellow handmaidens. During the Imperial Era, she carried a [[blaster rifle]] that was either a [[pulse cannon]] or [[DLT-20A blaster rifle]]. ==Behind the scenes== Sabé first appeared in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], portrayed by [[Wikipedia:English people|English]] actress [[Keira Knightley]]. Sabé was originally going to be filled by a [[Wikipedia:Stand-in|stand-in]], until casting director [[Robin Gurland]] came across Knightley, who bore a striking resemblance to [[Natalie Portman]], who portrayed Padmé Amidala in the film. Knightley's role was kept quiet by ''The Phantom Menace''{{'s}} marketing department in order to heighten the surprise of there being a decoy queen when the film was released and the queen's costumes were specifically designed to hide any height and shape differences between Portman and Knightley, so much in fact that even Portman's own mother could not distinguish between the two on set.{{InsiderCite|75|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of Star Wars)|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of ''Star Wars'')}} When asked years later about the role she had played in ''Star Wars'', Knightley was confused that her character's name was Sabé and not Padmé, as she was young during filming and has not viewed the movie since.
